Plots of poolinfo objects

Source: R/plot.R
plot.poolinfo.Rd

plot() shows one of the package's plots of a profile, a posterior fit, draws or a design. type chooses the plot, and most types call the plot function of the same name, so plot(fit, type = "pooling") is plot_pooling(fit).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("profile", "logit", "geometry", "decomposition", "gap", "concentration",
    "contributions"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("dashboard", "profile", "logit", "pooling", "functionals", "plane", "sigma",
    "gap", "concentration", "contributions"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_draws'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("dashboard", "profile", "logit", "pooling", "functionals", "plane", "sigma",
    "gap", "concentration", "contributions"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_design'
plot(x, type = c("imbalance", "sites", "target", "profile"), ...)

Arguments

x

A reliability_profile, reliability_posterior, reliability_draws or reliability_design object.

type

The plot:

  • for a profile, "profile" (the default), "logit", "geometry", "decomposition", "gap", "concentration" or "contributions".

  • for a posterior fit or draws, "dashboard" (the default), "profile", "logit", "pooling", "functionals", "plane", "sigma", "gap", "concentration" or "contributions".

  • for a design, "imbalance" (the default), "sites", "target" or "profile".

"logit" is plot_profile() with type = "logit", "sigma" is plot_sigma_scale(), "gap" is plot_gap_path(), and "imbalance", "sites" and "target" are the types of plot_design(); "profile" of a design shows the planned profile.

...

Further arguments of the plot function.

Value

A ggplot or patchwork object.

See also

plot_profile(), plot_dashboard(), plot_design(), and compare_profiles() for the plots of a comparison.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = school, data = eight_schools)
plot(fit)

plot(fit, type = "functionals")
